subject: GRB 260730B: CALET Gamma-Ray Burst Monitor detection
submitter: Yuta Kawakubo at Aoyama Gakuin University <kawakubo@phys.aoyama.ac.jp>
body:
Y. Shimizu (Kanagawa U), A. Yoshida, T. Sakamoto, S. Sugita, 
Y. Kawakubo (AGU), K. Yamaoka (Nagoya U), S. Nakahira (JAXA), 
Y. Asaoka (ICRR), S. Torii, Y. Akaike, K. Kobayashi (Waseda U), 
T. Tamura (Kanagawa U), N. Cannady (GSFC), M. L. Cherry (LSU), 
S. Ricciarini (U of Florence), P. S. Marrocchesi (U of Siena),
and the CALET collaboration:

The CALET Gamma-ray Burst Monitor (CGBM) detected GRB 260730B
at 13:13:50.13 UTC on 30 July 2026 (trigger #1469452426;
https://cgbm.calet.jp/cgbm_trigger/flight/1469452426/index.html).

No real-time CGBM GCN notice was distributed about this trigger because 
the real-time communication from the ISS was off (loss of signal).

This event was also reported by NuSTAR (Waratkar et al., GCN #45262) and 
AstroSat CZTI (Goyal et al., GCN #45265).

The burst signal was seen by all CGBM detectors.
The burst light curve shows a multi-peaked structure starting
at T-5.5 s, peaking at T+5.9 s, and ending at T+22.1 s.
The T90 and T50 durations measured with the SGM data are 17.1 +/- 0.9 s
and 6.1 +/- 0.9 s in the 40-1000 keV band, respectively.

The ground-processed light curve is available at:
https://cgbm.calet.jp/cgbm_trigger/ground/1469452426/

The CALET data used in this analysis were provided by
the Waseda CALET Operation Center located at Waseda University.
